events.title: Inflation crossed 50% (reached 78%)
events.detail: Consumer price inflation rose from 20.1% to 77.8%, crossing the 50% threshold.
events.source: derived: World Bank consumer price inflation
events.contested: The 50% line is a convention, not a natural boundary. Official inflation statistics are also among the most manipulated numbers governments publish, so the true figure may be higher than the one recorded here.

events.title: Military coup overthrows the Allende government
events.detail: The armed forces seized power, dissolving Congress and beginning a military government that lasted until 1990.
events.contested: The economic programme that followed is among the most polarised cases in the field. Supporters cite the post-1985 growth record; critics cite the 1982 collapse, the rise in inequality and poverty through the 1980s, and note that systematic human rights violations are not an economic trade-off to be netted off against GDP.
events.refs: ["Chilean National Commission on Truth and Reconciliation (Rettig Report, 1991)", "Ffrench-Davis, 'Economic Reforms in Chile' (2002)"]

events.title: Output collapse: GDP per capita fell 14%
events.detail: Real GDP per capita fell from 3,960 to 3,420 (constant 2015 US$) in a single year.
events.source: derived: World Bank GDP per capita
events.contested: A one-year collapse of this size usually has several causes at once - war, currency crisis, commodity price, or the end of a political order. This marker says it happened; it does not say why.

events.title: Democratic erosion: electoral democracy index fell 0.63 over 5 years
events.detail: From 0.70 in 1971 to 0.07 in 1976. Derived by detecting a sustained shift of at least 0.2 index points over 5 years; marked at the steepest year of the episode.
events.contested: V-Dem indices are aggregated expert judgements with published uncertainty intervals. A shift of this size is well outside the noise, but the exact year is a property of the detection rule, not a documented event.
